title: 302. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Finding Intervals of Increase and Decrease from Graphs
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Increasing Behavior of a Linear Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine from a linear graph whether the function is increasing or decreasing on a given interval.
questions.question: The graph of a function \(f\) is a straight line from \((-1,0)\) to \((3,8)\). Which statement correctly describes the behavior of the graph on \((-1,3)\)?
questions.explanation:
For a line through \((-1,0)\) and \((3,8)\), the slope is
\[
\frac{8-0}{3-(-1)}=\frac{8}{4}=2.
\]
Since the slope is positive, as \(x\) increases, \(f(x)\) increases. Therefore, the graph is increasing on \((-1,3)\).
questions.hint: Find the slope of the line and use the sign of the slope to decide whether the graph rises or falls.

questions.concept: Decreasing Behavior of a Linear Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine from a linear graph whether the function is increasing or decreasing on a given interval.
questions.question: The graph of a function \(g\) is a straight line from \((1,6)\) to \((4,0)\). Which statement correctly describes the behavior of the graph on \((1,4)\)?
questions.explanation:
The slope of the line is
\[
\frac{0-6}{4-1}=\frac{-6}{3}=-2.
\]
Because the slope is negative, as \(x\) increases, \(g(x)\) decreases. Hence the graph is decreasing on \((1,4)\).
questions.hint: Calculate the slope and check whether it is positive or negative.

questions.concept: Increasing Interval from a Turning Point
questions.learningObjective: Identify the interval of increase from a described turning point on a graph.
questions.question: The graph of a function \(f\) has a turning point at \(x=2\). It is decreasing on \((-\infty,2)\) and increasing on \((2,\infty)\). On which interval is the graph increasing?
questions.explanation: A turning point separates an interval of decrease from an interval of increase. Since the graph decreases before \(x=2\) and increases after \(x=2\), the interval of increase is \((2,\infty)\).
questions.hint: Look at the behavior on each side of the turning point \(x=2\).

questions.concept: Decreasing Interval from a Minimum Point
questions.learningObjective: Determine the interval of decrease from a described minimum point on a graph.
questions.question: The graph of a function \(f\) has its lowest point at \(x=-1\). It decreases on \((-\infty,-1)\) and increases on \((-1,\infty)\). On which interval is the graph decreasing?
questions.explanation: A minimum point occurs where the graph changes from decreasing to increasing. Since the graph decreases before \(x=-1\), the interval of decrease is \((-\infty,-1)\).
questions.hint: Identify the part of the graph that falls as \(x\) increases before the lowest point.

questions.concept: Increasing Interval in a Piecewise Linear Graph
questions.learningObjective: Identify an interval of increase from a piecewise linear graph given by joined points.
questions.question: A graph consists of line segments joining \((-2,0)\), \((0,4)\), \((2,0)\), and \((4,4)\). Which interval is an interval of increase of the graph?
questions.explanation: From \((0,4)\) to \((2,0)\), the \(y\)-values decrease, so the graph is decreasing on \((0,2)\). From \((2,0)\) to \((4,4)\), the \(y\)-values increase, so the graph is increasing on \((2,4)\). Therefore, \((2,4)\) is an interval of increase.
questions.hint: Compare the \(y\)-values as \(x\) increases along each line segment.

questions.concept: Decreasing Interval from Described Graph Behavior
questions.learningObjective: Identify the decreasing interval from a verbal description of a graph.
questions.question: The graph of a function \(f\) increases on \((-\infty,1)\), decreases on \((1,4)\), and increases on \((4,\infty)\). On which interval is the graph decreasing?
questions.explanation: The description states directly that the graph decreases on \((1,4)\). The interval \((4,\infty)\) is an interval of increase, so it is not correct.
questions.hint: Match the stated behavior with the interval where the graph falls.

questions.concept: Decreasing Interval from a Table of Graph Values
questions.learningObjective: Determine an interval of decrease from a table of values representing a graph.
questions.question:
The table gives points on the graph of \(f\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\\
\hline
f(x) & 2 & 5 & 3 & 1
\end{array}
\]
The graph consists of straight line segments joining consecutive listed points. On which interval is the graph decreasing?
questions.explanation: From \(x=0\) to \(x=1\), \(f(x)\) increases from \(2\) to \(5\). From \(x=1\) to \(x=3\), the values decrease: \(5\to 3\to 1\). Therefore, the graph is decreasing on \((1,3)\).
questions.hint: Look for the \(x\)-interval where the \(y\)-values become smaller as \(x\) increases.

questions.learningObjective: Use the sign of a cubic derivative to establish decrease on an entire interval.
questions.question: The graph of \(f(x)=-x^3+12x\) has a local minimum at \(x=-2\) and a local maximum at \(x=2\). On which interval is the graph decreasing?
questions.explanation: The derivative is \(f'(x)=12-3x^2\). It is positive for \(-2<x<2\) and negative for \(x>2\). Thus the graph increases on option A's interval and decreases on option B's interval.
questions.hint: Find where the rate of change of \(f\) is negative.

questions.concept: Identifying an Increasing Interval among Several Turning Points
questions.learningObjective: Select an interval of increase from a graph with multiple turning points.
questions.question: The graph of a function \(f\) has turning points at \(x=-3,-1,1,3\). It decreases on \((-\infty,-3)\), increases on \((-3,-1)\), decreases on \((-1,1)\), increases on \((1,3)\), and decreases on \((3,\infty)\). Which interval is an interval of increase?
questions.explanation: According to the given behavior, the graph decreases on \((-1,1)\), so option A is not an interval of increase. The graph increases on \((-3,-1)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the stated behavior with each interval and identify where the graph rises.

questions.concept: Complete Set of Increasing Intervals from a Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine the union of all intervals on which a described graph is increasing.
questions.question: The graph of a function \(f\) decreases on \((-\infty,-2)\), increases on \((-2,0)\), decreases on \((0,2)\), and increases on \((2,\infty)\). Which union of intervals is the set of all intervals on which the graph is increasing?
questions.explanation:
The graph is increasing on \((-2,0)\) and also increasing on \((2,\infty)\). Therefore, the complete set of increasing intervals is
\[
(-2,0)\cup(2,\infty).
\]
Option A lists intervals where the graph is decreasing, so it is incorrect.
questions.hint: Collect every interval from the description where the graph rises as \(x\) increases.
